title: Repair and Emergency Service Calls: Credit Base of the On-Time Credit for Comfort Club Members
content:
**Billing ruling.** On Repair and Emergency Service Calls, the credit base of the on-time credit for a customer with an active Comfort Club agreement under Comfort Club Maintenance Agreements is tied to the repair labor billed on the late call. The rate depends on whether the call's unit is protected under Harbison Protection Contracts. The records read are the member's agreement status, the protection contracts in active status and the unit each covers, and the amounts of the call's repair labor lines.

**Rule.** The credit base is figured this way:

- For a customer with an active Comfort Club agreement whose call concerns a unit covered by an active Harbison protection contract, it is 10 percent of the call's repair labor charges as billed.
- For any other customer with an active agreement, it is 5 percent of the call's repair labor charges as billed.
- In both of these cases it is rounded to the cent half up, and it is never less than the class's on-time credit.
- For every other customer it is the class's on-time credit.

In a call class whose on-time credit is zero, the credit base is zero.

| Active Comfort Club agreement | Call's unit under an active protection contract | Credit base |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 10 percent of the call's repair labor as billed, rounded, never below the class's on-time credit |
| Yes | No | 5 percent of the call's repair labor as billed, rounded, never below the class's on-time credit |
| No | Yes or no | The class's on-time credit |

## Worked figures (hypothetical calls, $25.00 class credit)

| Call's repair labor as billed | Member, unit protected | Member, unit not protected |
|---|---|---|
| $689.00 | 10 percent is $68.90 | 5 percent is $34.45 |
| $483.75 | 10 percent is $48.375, rounded to $48.38 | 5 percent is $24.1875, rounded to $24.19, raised to $25.00 |
| $153.00 | $15.30, raised to $25.00 | $7.65, raised to $25.00 |
| No repair labor | $25.00 | $25.00 |
